name: Fulde
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Reichardt, Charles Augustus Ludwig. 1876. Grammar of the Fulde language. With an appendix of some original traditions and portions of Scripture translated into Fulde: together with eight chapters of the book of Genesis. London: Church Missionary House. (Preface: 'The information was derived from natives of Futa Jallo'; principal informant Muhammed Sali Karamoko of Timbo, Fuuta Jaloo.)
catalog_locator: Part I, Chapter V 'The Accentuation', §14, rules (1)-(8) and 'Conclusion', pp. 14-17 (archive.org copy A)
catalog_quote: §. 14. To establish exact and binding definitions for the intonation of the Fulde, is rather a difficult undertaking. The cases in which the tone syllable can be defined by rules are the following :— (1). The position of the tone syllable in Fulde words varies between the antepenult and the penult, or in other words, between the second and third syllables if counting from the end of the word. (2). If a word contains a syllable with a long vowel, the accent rests thereon; diphthongs are, however, not necessarily equal to long vowels ... (3). A certain number of words ... allow two long syllables to occur in one and the same word; in this case the accent rests upon that of the long vowels, that is, next to the end of the word ... (4). Upon the penult is the accentuation in all disyllabic words, whether the vowel be short or long ... (6). Upon the ante penult is the tone in many pollysyllabic words of purely short syllables; to this class belong many nouns ... (7). ... the tone has to make a move forward in all nouns that are increased by the article ... as: légal = legángal ... (8). Accentuation upon the ultima occurs but seldom. ... Conclusion:—The above given rules for the accentuation may hold good in the majority of cases; to enter upon the many deviations is impossible.
world_status: statement found in an open source

Chapter V 'THE ACCENTUATION', sect. 14 is exactly where the compiler says. The quoted passage is verbatim on the scan: p.14 '§. 14. To establish exact and binding definitions for the intonation of the Fulde, is rather a difficult undertaking. The cases in which the tone syllable can be defined by rules are the following:— (1). The position of the tone syllable in Fulde words varies' / p.15 'between the antepenult and the penult, or in other words, between the second and third syllables if counting fr…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Accent ('tone syllable') falls within a two-syllable window (penult or antepenult): a syllable with a long vowel attracts the accent (if two long syllables, the one nearer the word end, rule 3); disyllables are accented on the penult (i.e. initial); polysyllables consisting only of short syllables are accented on the antepenult (deftere, amude, windudo); adding class/definite suffixes (-ngal, -ngol, -ngu..) or heavy plural suffixes moves the accent rightward onto the new penult (légal > legángal); final-syllable accent is rare.
new_statements.exceptions: Ultima accent 'but seldom': contracted 1st-conj. negative present (min aratá > ará, andatá > andá), some derived-conjugation finals (mi windaná, holtirá), the greeting kisiyé; numerals 6-9 are antepenult (jédidi, jétati, jénai) unlike other numerals/adjectives/adverbs (penult); the 'light' suffix -ndu behaves differently from other class suffixes; author concedes 'the many deviations' and marks accent in all texts.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level accent of citation/isolated word forms, including suffixed definite and plural forms; author uses 'intonation/tone syllable/accent' interchangeably for word accent (1876 terminology), not lexical tone. Data from Futa Jallo (Timbo) speakers resident in Sierra Leone, collected 1850s.
new_statements.identity_note: Reichardt 1876 states in the Preface that 'The information was derived from natives of Futa Jallo' (principal informant Muhammed Sali Karamoko of Timbo, resident in Sierra Leone, d. 1859), i.e. Fuuta Jaloo Pular = pula1262; only the appended Genesis chapters (from Baikie) are Sokoto/Adamawa Fulfulde and are not the basis of the grammar. Diallo 2015 and Caudill & Diallo 2000 are explicitly Fouta Djallon/Fuuta Jallon Pular. Apel 2020 is Guinean Pular (Dalaba + diaspora speakers). Note Glottolog also files Gaden 1913-14 'Le Poular, dialecte peul du Fouta sénégalais' under pula1262, but that work describes Fuuta Tooro Pulaar (pula1263) and was not used.

sources.citation: Gaden, Henri (1913-1914). Le Poular: Dialecte Peul de Fouta Sénégalais. Paris: Éditeur Ernest Leroux. v+338+xii+263 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Gaden describes 'le dialecte peul parlé au Fouta sénégalais', the Toucouleur speech of the Lâo (Fuuta Tooro, Senegal), which Glottolog files as Pulaar [pula1263, fuc] with Toucouleur [touc1238] as its dialect, not Pular of Fuuta Jaloo [pula1262]. Even taken as evidence, it neither confirms nor refutes Reichardt's weight-sensitive antepenult/penult rule for Fulde: it agrees that accent and vowel length are linked (accent marked on long vowels; accent lengthens its vowel) but reports final-vowel accent in negative tenses and states that the general rule is undetermined.

sources.note: No placement rule. 'Spelling and pronunciation': 'double consonants (bb, cc, etc.) indicate a stressed consonant' (i.e. gemination); Food chapter notes weelaa 'hungry' vs welaa 'tastes good' differ by 'a slightly different stress pattern in pronunciation'. Nothing on where word stress falls.
